verdict.rationale: Notion documents headless, non-interactive access through its REST API, which can read, create, and update nearly everything in a workspace. It also documents personal access tokens for scripts and CLI workflows, and static-token internal connections described as ideal for custom automations, so unattended scripted runs are supported. However, there is no documented CI-specific guidance, no official headless CLI or runner, and no hands-on corroboration of CI use. missing for 10: CI pipeline documentation/examples, official CLI or headless runner, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Personal access tokens (PATs) are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLI workflows, Workers, and tools that should act as one Notion user.
Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace and use a static API token. They're ideal for custom automations and workflows
With the REST API, you can read, create, and update nearly everything in a workspace — pages, databases, users, comments, and more.
